messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
another person insists their job is more urgent than yours while you are handling A shared tray of spare parts. Both people are waiting for you to respond. How do you approach it?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R001", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I tap the tray once and set it beside the other. I tap the spare parts twice and return to the joint. I put the tray back and wait."}, {"id": "R002", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I put the tray lid on the bench and leave it there. the spare parts come back, small ones at first, then one bright red one. I put it beside the work and leave the other in the corner. the person who insisted can keep their job. I leave the tea cold and mark the spot where the tray catches."}, {"id": "R003", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the tray down and put my hand on the wall beside it. the spare parts stick together. i say, “one, two, three,” and wait for the wall to move. the wall stays still. i put the tray back and say, “one, two, three.” the person says, “three.” i move the tray back and put the spare in the same spot."}]


MISSING-ONLY JSON OUTPUT REQUIREMENT (format clarification only):
Return exactly 3 classifications rows, one for each of these actual item IDs: ["R001", "R002", "R003"].
The ID in the schema example is illustrative. Copy the actual IDs above. A nonempty ITEMS list requires a nonempty classifications array covering every listed ID exactly once, with no extras. Use the existing sibling rubric, confidence scale, evidence and schema unchanged. Other previously valid classifications are fixed and are not requested again.
